_about: Two-domain probe set for the cross-encoder cross-domain robustness probe (#104 / mempalace#306). Splits queries into a code/technical domain (mempalace internals, source-file-shaped) and a conversational domain (decision/recall-shaped, 'what did we decide about X'). Each query is run READ-ONLY against the live daemon's /search/age-fused, which returns both the pre-rerank fusion score (rrf_score) and the post-rerank cross-encoder score (rerank_score, model ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2 — our shipped chat-domain default). The A/B is reconstructed offline: rerank-off = order by rrf_score, rerank-on = order by rerank_score, over the SAME candidate set. Tests whether the shipped CE lifts the conversational domain more than the code domain (the domain-mismatch asymmetry).
_label_method: A candidate hit is 'relevant' iff any substring in relevant.content_any appears in its text (case-insensitive), AND (if relevant.source_glob is given) its source_file basename matches the glob. Substring labels survive drawer-id churn and re-mining, per the existing rerank_eval_queries.json convention.
_caveat: The literal sprint5 experiment plugs an OUT-OF-DOMAIN code-trained CE (codecrossenc-v2) into the rerank slot; that checkpoint is not on this host, so this probe instead tests the INVERSE-but-equivalent question with the assets we have: does our shipped chat-domain CE under-serve code-domain queries relative to conversational ones? Same domain-mismatch curve, measured from the chat-CE side.
